asDecan.p: Libra gets cut into three slices of ten degrees, called decans, and each slice has its own planet and its own small card. Your Sun sits somewhere between 20 and 29 degrees of Libra, the last slice, and in the old Chaldean order that one goes to Jupiter. Jupiter has no special standing in Libra. It's a visitor, so it minds its manners and takes on the tone of the house, and the house belongs to Venus, the sign's ruler. Venus wants things pleasant and fair, and Jupiter makes whatever it touches a bit bigger and more generous, so you end up with a Libra that has more room in it. The slice before yours is the Three of Swords, Saturn, where Libra learns about fairness the hard way. Before that comes the Two, the Moon, holding two choices and not picking. You come straight after the heartbreak card, which is probably why yours shows a figure lying down to rest. You're also at the very end of the sign, already leaning toward Scorpio, and that puts some depth under the easy manner.

You're the one people ring after the argument, and you're good at it. Your sister and your mum fall out over who's hosting Christmas, and somehow it's you on the phone to each of them in turn, making it sound a bit less final than it did an hour ago. After a meeting that went badly, you're the one who sends the friendly email that gets everybody talking again. You also need a surprising amount of quiet for someone so sociable. A Saturday with nothing in the diary is how you get back to level after a week of being nice to everyone, and you guard it more fiercely than you let on. When a text comes in that's a bit sharp, you leave it overnight before you answer. By morning you've usually found the generous way to read it, and to be honest you're usually right.

The less obvious gift is that you give other people permission to stop. Plenty of people are kind, but Jupiter in this slice makes you generous with time and slack, which is rarer. A friend is running on fumes, caring for a parent and working full time, and you're the one who says go home, I'll sort the school pickup, and means it so plainly that they actually go. At work you notice the colleague who hasn't taken leave in eighteen months and quietly mention it to the right person. You don't make a speech about self-care. You just make resting look normal, because you do it yourself without apologising, and people around you start doing it too. I see this a lot with late Libra Suns. The office gets calmer and nobody can quite say why.

The pause is your strength, and it can also turn into a very comfortable place to hide. Jupiter is an optimist, and with Venus setting the tone the optimism leans toward hoping things will settle by themselves if nobody pushes. Sometimes they do. Often they don't. The conversation with your partner about money gets parked in autumn and it's still parked the following winter, sitting there politely. The friend who keeps cancelling on you never hears that it bothers you, so they keep doing it. There's a spending side too, because Jupiter and Venus together like comfort. The good sheets, the long lunch, the weekend away to recover from a week that wasn't that bad. None of that is wrong on its own. It's worth noticing when rest has quietly become the thing you do so you don't have to decide.

Under strain you go polite first. Something goes badly wrong, a redundancy, a friendship that ends, a family row you couldn't smooth over, and for the first few days you're gracious to everyone and fine, thanks, really. About a week later you disappear. Early nights, phone face down, the curtains half shut on a Sunday afternoon. That's the Four of Swords doing its job, and it's genuinely how you recover, but the people close to you often didn't see it coming, because on the surface you were coping beautifully. Your partner ends up guessing, and guessing wrong. What helps is telling one person that you're going quiet and roughly for how long. Sleep, plain food, a walk somewhere with trees. And then someone you trust who comes round and doesn't need you to be pleasant while they're there.

You're quick to forgive, and in this slice it's big forgiveness, Jupiter-sized. A partner says something cruel in a fight and by the next morning you've put it down, which is lovely, except that sometimes you've put it down before they've actually said sorry. Over a few years that teaches someone they don't need to. The Scorpio edge of your degrees shows up here as well. You look easygoing and you want more depth than you let on, and the relationships that last tend to be with people who can sit through a long, honest conversation without getting defensive. You also need someone who doesn't take your quiet weekends personally. Tell them early, before they've had the chance to worry, that when you disappear into the couch for a day it isn't about them.

Justice is your Sun card, and this slice gives it a particular kind of job to do. The earlier Libra decans weigh things up. You're better at what happens after the verdict, when people have to go on working together. Mediation, HR, family law, hospitality, nursing, running a team through a merger or a restructure, any role where people turn up rattled and need to leave steadier. You have a long view at work that comes from Jupiter, and you don't panic about one bad quarter. The catch is pace. You do well in bursts and then need real recovery, and a job with no slack in it wears you down faster than it would most people. Take your full annual leave, actually take it, and try to book it before you're desperate for it.

At twenty this decan usually shows up as saying yes to everything and everyone, being the peacemaker in every share house and friendship group, and then crashing flat for a week and not really knowing why. The rest happens, but only when the body forces it. By the mid-thirties most people with a Sun here have learnt to schedule the quiet on purpose, and to say no a bit earlier. They're usually a lot less tired and a little less popular, and fine with that. The fifties often bring the role of the calm older friend, the one people visit when their own lives have got too loud. The thing to watch then is withdrawing a bit too comfortably, letting the quiet get so pleasant that you stop turning up to things you'd actually enjoy.

Pick one evening a week and put it in your calendar as unavailable, with no reason given. On that evening the phone goes in another room from dinner until bed. Don't fill it with chores or catch-up emails. Lie on the floor, read, have a bath, do nothing much. If someone asks you to do something that night, say you've already got plans, because you have. After a month, notice how much easier the other six evenings feel.
